title: A Sharp Joint Bias-Energy Envelope for Radial Clipping
summary: Radial clipping does two things at once: it removes the part of a vector outside a ball and retains a bounded vector inside the ball. The removed part produces bias, while the squared norm of the retained part produces energy. We determine the exact joint price of these effects when only a $p$-moment, $1<p\le2$, is available. The problem turns out to be one-dimensional: everything is decided by the position of one point along a ray. At $α=pβ$, the extremal configuration changes.
